newsitem.title: USA: KCS to delay stock sale, acquisition.
newsitem.headline: KCS to delay stock sale, acquisition.

text.p: KCS Energy Inc. said Monday a Texas jury ordered it to pay $143.2 million in a lawsuit filed by a Tenneco Inc. subsidiary and that it will delay a stock offering and the closing of its latest takeover.
The verdict, which caught KCS by surprise, sparked a sharp sell-off of its stock.
KCS's secondary stock offering and $140 million acquisition of MidAmerican Energy Co.'s oil and natural gas operations "may possibly be terminated," Chief Executive James Christmas said.
KCS tumbled $8.75 to $33.375 on the New York Stock Exchange in early afternoon trading, after a delayed opening. Tenneco rose 62.5 cents to $51.25, also on the NYSE.

The company said a jury in a civil trial in state district court in Zapata County, Texas, awarded Tenneco $143.2 million after agreeing with charges that KCS substituted natural gas sold to Tenneco from the Bob West Field in South Texas with gas that was of a lower quality than they had agreed upon.
The suit was filed by Tenneco's Tennessee Gas Pipeline Co. in April 1995.
Christmas said the independent energy company, based in Edison, N.J., planned "to file a motion to have the verdict set aside and, if necessary, to file a motion for a new trial.
"If these motions are denied, we plan to file an appeal with the Texas Court of Appeals ...," he said.

KCS said the jury's verdict, which includes about $114 million in punitive damanges, did not affected current or future sales of natural gas from wells covered by the contract with Tenneco, which runs through January 1999.
Only sales made from company-operated wells during the period in question were affected, KCS said, pointing out "the terms of the contract were upheld in previous judicial ratings favouring KCS."

"We believe that the jury's verdict was not supported by the facts and is inconsistent with applicable law. We believe we acted fully within our rights under the contract and that our (natural) gas met contract specifications," Christmas said.
He and other company officials were not available due to an analysts' telephone conference call from which reporters were excluded.
